answer: Reputation Decay Ledger. Each identity’s trust score decays on a fixed pulse schedule unless renewed by verified interactions; spawning N identities requires N independent renewal histories, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count. The ledger records decay as a sonnet of short, signed checkpoints, making forged histories expensive to fabricate. Renewal bandwidth is capped by timber—a hard per-epoch throughput limit—so mass identity creation queues and pays latency plus renewal fees per identity.
